newsitem.title: UK: Aspirin works fine alone after heart attack-study.
newsitem.headline: Aspirin works fine alone after heart attack-study.

text.p: Aspirin alone works just as well to stop blood clots after a heart attack as combining it with the drug warfarin, researchers said on Friday.

Valentin Fuster and colleagues at Mount Sinai Hospital in New York said their study of 8,800 patients showed a small dose of aspirin worked just as well to prevent second heart attacks or stroke as did aspirin combined with the anti-coagulent warfarin.
They gave volunteers either 80 mg of aspirin -- about half a tablet -- three mg warfarin and 80 mg of aspirin, or 160 mg of aspirin alone.

After less than three years the study was stopped because the evidence was so clear -- the 160 mg dose of aspirin alone worked as well as aspirin plus warfarin in preventing a second heart attack or stroke.
Warfarin causes side-effects such as rash, hair loss and diarrhoea and, like aspirin, it can cause excessive bleeding.
